Use of generative AI in this project

Source: AI_USE.md

Last reviewed: 2026-11-12. Maintainer: Michael S. Zens.

This statement describes how a generative AI assistant (Anthropic’s Claude, used through the Claude Code command-line tool) has been used in developing the curveR packages and the I-SPI application, and how its output is checked. It follows the principle that a project should say plainly what AI did, what people did, and who is accountable.

Summary

Tool Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code; model versions are recorded in the working notes, not in commits
Where it was used (1) refining the user interfaces of I-SPI; (2) reviewing and checking the integrity of the statistical analysis that processes assay responses (calibration curves, precision weights, censoring); (3) drafting code, tests and documentation under direction
Where it was not used choosing scientific questions or study designs; interpreting results for any publication; handling participant-level data outside the access controls of the institution
Accountability The maintainer reviews and is responsible for every change that is merged. AI is not an author of the software or of any analysis

What the assistant did

  • User interface refinement (I-SPI). Proposed and implemented layout, labelling, help text and navigation changes in the Shiny application, which the maintainer reviewed in the running application.
  • Statistical integrity review. Re-derived and challenged the variance models used to weight assay measurements, for example the move from a multiplicative to an additive measurement-error model, the treatment of censored (out-of-range) samples, and the handling of dilution scales. Findings were checked by simulation with known true values and are kept as automated tests (tests/testthat).
  • Engineering. Wrote code, database migrations, tests and documentation (vignettes, glossary, data dictionary) from instructions given by the maintainer.

What people did

  • Set the scientific goals and requirements, for instance that existing behaviour and the existing test suite must remain unchanged, and that a new statistical model is opt-in until it has been validated.
  • Decided which statistical approach to adopt and which results to trust.
  • Reviewed all diffs, approved every commit, release and database change, and operated the deployed systems.
  • Hold all credentials. The assistant works with a restricted set of permissions and does not store secrets in repositories.

How output is verified

  1. Automated tests. The unit tests of each package, including tests that pin pre-existing behaviour, must pass unmodified before a change is merged.
  2. Simulation with ground truth. Statistical claims are checked on simulated data where the true answer is known (for example, recovering a known group difference, bias of weighted versus unweighted means).
  3. End-to-end checks on disposable infrastructure. Database changes are rehearsed on a throwaway database; a snapshot of the affected rows is taken before any overwrite, and a rollback path exists.
  4. Independent package checks. R CMD check with no errors or warnings before each release.
  5. Human review. Nothing reaches the public repositories or the deployed application without the maintainer approving it.

Assistant output can be wrong in plausible-sounding ways. Where the documentation makes a numerical claim, the number is produced by code in the same document.

Data and privacy

The assistant runs on the maintainer’s workstation and can read the files and database queries the maintainer permits during a session; content it reads is processed by the AI provider’s service. The maintainer limits that access to what the task needs and applies the institution’s rules for research data. Exports that contain patient identifiers (for example weight snapshots taken before a database change) are stored outside the repositories, and credentials are kept in files that are excluded from version control.

Reproducibility and provenance

Release notes and the git history record what changed and when. The packages’ NEWS.md files list each change. Commits are authored by the maintainer and do not carry an AI co-author trailer; this document is the project’s disclosure instead.

Contact

Questions about the use of AI in this project or about a specific analytic decision: open an issue in the relevant repository or contact the maintainer.
